title: peaks
summary: Generate the standard peaks test surface in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: RunMat may select the active provider automatically for generated grids and equal-shape resident coordinate inputs. Explicit gpuArray coordinate or grid-size input is a separately declared RunMat extension because the public compatibility target does not document GPU-array support.

description:
`peaks(n)` evaluates the standard peaks function over an n×n grid spanning [-3, 3] × [-3, 3]:

```
Z = 3*(1-x)^2 * exp(-x^2 - (y+1)^2)
    - 10*(x/5 - x^3 - y^5) * exp(-x^2 - y^2)
    - 1/3 * exp(-(x+1)^2 - y^2)
```

It is commonly used to demonstrate 3-D surface plots. Formula and default grid size follow MATLAB semantics.
behaviors: `peaks` with no arguments returns a 49×49 matrix (MATLAB default).

`peaks(n)` requires a scalar integer greater than one and returns an n×n matrix evaluated on an n-point grid from -3 to 3 on both axes. A typed-integer scalar n is a RunMat extension decoded structurally from native storage.
`peaks(X, Y)` accepts mutually compatible coordinate sizes and returns a broadcast Z matrix.
`[X, Y, Z] = peaks(Xm,Ym)` returns X and Y equal to the original coordinates, including their exact integer classes and wide values, while Z is computed in the floating peaks formula domain.
When exactly two outputs are requested, `[X, Y] = peaks(n)` returns only the coordinate grids without Z.

faqs.question: Why is the default size 49?
faqs.answer: MATLAB chose 49 as the default grid size for `peaks`. RunMat matches this specification.

faqs.question: Can I get the coordinate grids back as well as Z?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use `[X, Y, Z] = peaks(n)` to retrieve all three matrices.

faqs.question: How do I move the result to the GPU?
faqs.answer: RunMat can select the active provider automatically for generated grids. Explicit gpuArray inputs are a declared RunMat extension and are rejected in strict MATLAB compatibility mode.

faqs.question: What values are valid for scalar `n`?
faqs.answer: Scalar `n` must be an integer greater than one.

gpu_residency: `peaks` always runs on the host CPU today. If you need the result on the GPU, wrap the call in `gpuArray(...)`.
gpu_behavior: RunMat computes `peaks` on the host and returns a host tensor. No acceleration provider hooks are defined for this builtin.
